CURRENT ITERATION REQUEST:

# Iteration 01 — Backend foundation

We are building a scalable University Partnership Management System.

For this iteration work ONLY on the Django REST Framework backend.
Do NOT build the Vue frontend yet.

The platform will eventually become a large system used by university staff, international relations, deans, finance, rectorate and other departments. Keep the first iteration small, but design the data model so future features can be added without redesigning Organization and Agreement.

## Goal
Create a working Django REST Framework backend for managing partner organizations, agreements, contacts, documents and activities.

Use SQLite for this development iteration.
Create the Django project inside `workspace/backend` and create a Django app named `partnerships`.

## Models

### Organization
Fields:
- name
- organization_type: UNIVERSITY, COMPANY, GOVERNMENT, NGO, OTHER
- country
- website
- description
- is_public
- created_by
- updated_by
- created_at
- updated_at

One organization can have many agreements.
Example: Huawei -> MoU 2024, Huawei ICT Academy, Cooperation Agreement 2026.

### Agreement
Fields:
- organization: ForeignKey to Organization
- title
- agreement_type: MOU, MOA, ACADEMY, PARTNERSHIP, EXCHANGE, NDA, OTHER
- status: DRAFT, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, EXPIRED, UNDER_RENEWAL
- description
- signed_date
- start_date
- expiration_date
- created_by
- updated_by
- created_at
- updated_at

Do not assume only one agreement per organization.

### Contact
Fields:
- full_name
- organization: nullable ForeignKey to Organization
- position
- email
- phone
- notes
- created_at
- updated_at

A Contact can represent a partner employee or an internal university employee. Internal contacts may have organization = null.

### AgreementContact
Fields:
- agreement: ForeignKey
- contact: ForeignKey
- side: OUR_SIDE or PARTNER_SIDE
- role
- is_primary

Use this model so an agreement can have multiple contacts on both sides.

### Document
Fields:
- agreement: ForeignKey
- title
- document_type
- file
- description
- uploaded_by
- uploaded_at

An Agreement can have unlimited documents. Do not store one document directly on Agreement.

### Activity
Fields:
- agreement: ForeignKey
- title
- activity_date
- description
- created_by
- updated_by
- created_at
- updated_at

An Agreement can have unlimited activities.

## Django Admin
Register all models with useful `list_display`, `search_fields`, and `list_filter`.

## REST API
Install and configure Django REST Framework.
Create serializers and ModelViewSets.
Create authenticated internal endpoints:
- /api/organizations/
- /api/agreements/
- /api/contacts/
- /api/agreement-contacts/
- /api/documents/
- /api/activities/

For this iteration, Django session authentication and DRF default authentication are sufficient. Do not implement JWT yet.

## Public API
Create `GET /api/public/organizations/`.
This endpoint must allow unauthenticated access, be read-only, and expose only:
- id
- name
- organization_type
- country
- website

Do not expose contacts, documents, descriptions, users, created_by or updated_by.

## Media uploads
Configure MEDIA_ROOT and MEDIA_URL correctly for local development. Documents must upload into a sensible folder structure.

## Audit-ready foundation
Keep created_by, updated_by, created_at and updated_at on core models where requested. We will add full audit history later.

Do NOT implement Contribution, finance, analytics, notifications or audit history yet. The architecture must allow them later without redesigning Organization and Agreement.

## Validation
Create and run migrations. Run `python manage.py check`. Fix all errors that can be fixed.

## Documentation
Create `workspace/backend/README.md` with exact local commands to create a virtual environment, install dependencies, migrate, create a superuser and runserver. Also document the public and internal endpoints.

## Scope guard
BACKEND ONLY. Do not create Vue, frontend, dashboards, JWT, finance, analytics, notifications or advanced roles. Finish only this backend foundation and leave it clean and runnable.


Implement the requested iteration in workspace/.
Rules:
- Inspect existing files before changing anything.
- Make real file changes; do not only explain.
- Preserve existing working functionality.
- Respect the scope of this iteration.
- If the iteration explicitly says backend-only, do not create Vue/frontend code.
- Run relevant checks after implementation.
- Never put secrets in source code.
1. Inspect the repository before making any change, as required. Use list_files on workspace/ and identify whether workspace/backend already exists, whether a Django project, virtual environment, dependency manifest, migrations, database, or unrelated frontend code is present. Use read_file on all existing project files that may be affected, especially manage.py, settings.py, root URLs, requirements files, and any existing app files. Preserve working functionality and adapt an existing backend rather than blindly overwriting it.

2. Establish the backend project only under workspace/backend. If no Django project exists, use RunCommandTool from workspace/ to create backend/ and initialize the project and partnerships application (for example, install dependencies in the active development environment if needed, then run django-admin startproject config backend and python manage.py startapp partnerships from backend/). If a project exists, verify that the project package and manage.py are correctly located under backend/ and create only the missing partnerships app pieces.

3. Add a minimal dependency declaration suitable for reproducible setup, such as backend/requirements.txt, containing Django and djangorestframework with sensible compatible version bounds or pinned versions consistent with the installed environment. Do not add JWT packages, frontend packages, finance/analytics packages, or secret-bearing configuration.

4. Update Django settings carefully. Add rest_framework and partnerships to INSTALLED_APPS while retaining Django defaults. Keep the SQLite DATABASES configuration, using BASE_DIR / db.sqlite3. Set MEDIA_URL = '/media/' and MEDIA_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'media'. Configure REST_FRAMEWORK default authentication using SessionAuthentication and Django’s normal DRF defaults, and default permission behavior so internal API endpoints require authenticated users (either global IsAuthenticated with explicit public override, or IsAuthenticated assigned on each internal viewset). Do not configure JWT. Keep SECRET_KEY development-safe without committing real credentials; retain the generated local development key if creating a standard Django project.

5. Design and implement partnerships/models.py with explicit TextChoices for all prescribed enumerations. Create Organization with name, organization_type choices UNIVERSITY/COMPANY/GOVERNMENT/NGO/OTHER, country, website, description, is_public, created_by, updated_by, created_at, and updated_at. Create Agreement with a ForeignKey to Organization and title, agreement_type choices MOU/MOA/ACADEMY/PARTNERSHIP/EXCHANGE/NDA/OTHER, status choices DRAFT/ACTIVE/INACTIVE/EXPIRED/UNDER_RENEWAL, description, signed_date, start_date, expiration_date, created_by, updated_by, created_at, and updated_at. Ensure organization is not made unique and use related_name values appropriate for future extension.

6. Complete the remaining normalized models without placing contacts, documents, or activities directly on Agreement. Implement Contact with nullable/blankable organization ForeignKey, full_name, position, email, phone, notes, created_at, and updated_at. Implement AgreementContact as the explicit many-to-many-through relationship with agreement ForeignKey, contact ForeignKey, side choices OUR_SIDE/PARTNER_SIDE, role, and is_primary. Implement Document with agreement ForeignKey, title, document_type, file, description, uploaded_by, and uploaded_at. Implement Activity with agreement ForeignKey, title, activity_date, description, created_by, updated_by, created_at, and updated_at.

7. Use appropriate field types and null/blank semantics: URLField for website, EmailField for email, DateField for agreement dates and activity_date, FileField for document files, DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True) and DateTimeField(auto_now=True) for requested timestamps, and nullable SET_NULL user ForeignKeys for audit/upload fields so historical records remain valid if a user is removed. Add upload_to callable or a static agreement-oriented path such as agreements/%Y/%m/ so uploaded files are organized sensibly. Add readable __str__ methods. Add only modest integrity constraints that match the requirements, such as a uniqueness constraint preventing duplicate agreement-contact links if desired; do not invent advanced role, audit-history, financial, or contribution models.

8. Create and inspect migrations. Run python manage.py makemigrations partnerships from workspace/backend, read the generated migration to ensure all six tables, field choices, nullable Contact.organization, all audit fields, and relationships match the specification, then run python manage.py migrate. Do not hand-edit an already-valid migration unless necessary.

9. Implement partnerships/admin.py and register all six models. For every model, provide useful list_display, search_fields, and list_filter appropriate to its fields: organization type/public status and timestamps for organizations; type/status/organization/dates for agreements; organization for contacts; agreement/side/primary for AgreementContact; agreement/document_type/uploaded date for Document; agreement/activity_date for Activity. Include autocomplete_fields or raw-ID-friendly widgets for relationships when useful. Ensure search fields use relationship lookups correctly and do not reference nonexistent columns.

10. Implement partnerships/serializers.py. Provide ModelSerializers for Organization, Agreement, Contact, AgreementContact, Document, and Activity. Expose the required model fields to authenticated internal users, mark created_by, updated_by, uploaded_by, created_at, updated_at, and uploaded_at read-only where the server manages them, and let relationship primary keys be writable. Define a dedicated PublicOrganizationSerializer whose Meta.fields is exactly id, name, organization_type, country, website and nothing else. Avoid nested serializers or extra public fields that could accidentally disclose descriptions, users, contacts, or documents.

11. Implement partnerships/views.py using ModelViewSet classes for all six internal resources. Protect every internal viewset with IsAuthenticated. In perform_create, set created_by for Organization, Agreement, and Activity from request.user, set uploaded_by for Document, and leave models that do not request creator fields unchanged. In perform_update, set updated_by for Organization, Agreement, and Activity from request.user. Preserve existing owner values when appropriate and never trust audit-user values supplied in request data. Use multipart-capable parsers (MultiPartParser/FormParser, optionally JSONParser) on the Document viewset so actual file uploads work.

12. Implement the public organizations endpoint as a read-only DRF endpoint/viewset using PublicOrganizationSerializer and AllowAny. Limit its queryset to Organization objects with is_public=True, so the endpoint is genuinely public only for organizations intentionally marked public. Allow GET list and optionally retrieve through a read-only router route, but ensure POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE cannot be performed anonymously or at all through this public endpoint.

13. Add partnerships/urls.py with a DRF DefaultRouter registration whose route basenames produce precisely organizations, agreements, contacts, agreement-contacts, documents, and activities under /api/. Add a separate public route for GET /api/public/organizations/ (and only any conventional trailing-slash behavior supplied by Django). Include these URLs from the project’s root urls.py at api/. In development URL patterns, append static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT) under DEBUG so uploaded files are locally served. Retain Django admin at /admin/.

14. Add backend/README.md with exact commands run from workspace/backend: create and activate a virtual environment for common local shells as appropriate, install requirements, run migrations, create a superuser, and start runserver. State the admin URL, all authenticated internal endpoints, the unauthenticated read-only public endpoint, session-authentication expectation, multipart document upload expectation, SQLite usage, and local media location. Do not document unimplemented frontend/JWT/features.

15. Run validation from workspace/backend: python manage.py makemigrations --check, python manage.py migrate, python manage.py check, and python manage.py test. If check or tests identify issues, inspect the named files with ReadFileTool, correct only iteration-relevant code with WriteFileTool, and rerun until clean.

16. Perform focused smoke validation using Django’s shell or an APIClient-based temporary/scripted check: create a user; verify unauthenticated GET /api/organizations/ receives a 401/403; verify authenticated requests can create and retrieve an organization, agreement, nullable-organization contact, AgreementContact, activity, and multipart Document; verify created_by/updated_by/uploaded_by are server-assigned; verify public GET includes only public organizations; verify its response keys are exactly the five permitted keys; and verify a public write is rejected. Do not leave test artifacts or credentials in source code.

17. Inspect the final file tree with list_files and the key changed files with read_file. Confirm there is no Vue/frontend application, dashboard, JWT configuration, finance, analytics, notification, Contribution, advanced-role, or audit-history implementation. Report a concise implementation summary, changed files, commands/checks run and their successful outcomes, plus any non-fixable environment limitation only if encountered.

CURRENT ITERATION

# Iteration 01C — Focused schema repair

This is an EXISTING Django REST Framework backend.

Do NOT regenerate the project.
Do NOT rewrite unrelated files.
Do NOT build frontend.
Do NOT redesign the architecture.

The backend is already running successfully with:

python manage.py runserver

and:

python manage.py check

currently passes.

We have already run deterministic verification and found ONLY these schema/migration problems.

## Required fixes

### 1. Document model

The Document model currently lacks:

- document_type
- description

It must contain at least:

- agreement
- title
- document_type
- file
- description
- uploaded_by
- uploaded_at

Add the missing fields safely.

`document_type` may be a CharField.

For now do not overengineer document type choices.

`description` may be blank.

Important:
The current migration state has a problem adding `uploaded_at` with `auto_now_add=True`.

Fix this safely without deleting the database or old migrations.

Prefer an additive/backward-compatible migration.

Do NOT delete db.sqlite3.

Do NOT edit already-applied migration history unless absolutely unavoidable.

### 2. Activity model

The Activity model currently lacks:

- title
- updated_by
- updated_at

It must contain at least:

- agreement
- title
- activity_date
- description
- created_by
- updated_by
- created_at
- updated_at

The existing activity_type field may remain.

Add missing fields safely.

### 3. Admin

Inspect admin.py.

Make sure it references ONLY fields that actually exist after the schema repair.

Do not redesign admin unnecessarily.

### 4. Serializers

Inspect serializers.py.

Update Document and Activity serializers only if required by the repaired model fields.

Preserve existing API behavior.

### 5. Migrations

After model changes:

Run:

python manage.py makemigrations
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py check
python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run --noinput

All must complete successfully.

If there is an interactive migration issue, solve it safely using defaults or nullable transitional fields.

Do not wait for interactive input.

### 6. Scope guard

Do NOT implement:

- Vue
- JWT
- finance
- contributions
- analytics
- dashboards
- notifications
- advanced roles
- new architecture

Make only the smallest patch required.

Stop immediately after all requested checks pass.

Final response must include:

CHANGED FILES
CHECKS RUN
REMAINING BLOCKERS
ITERATION STATUS: COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE

RULES
1. Inspect current workspace first.
2. Use environment_info before shell commands.
3. Existing repository: do not regenerate working parts.
4. Make the minimum changes required.
5. Never delete db.sqlite3, migrations, uploads, or working features unless explicitly requested.
6. Do not add unrelated future features.
7. Run requested checks.
8. If a check fails, make a focused fix and rerun it.
9. Stop when scope passes.
10. Final answer: CHANGED FILES, CHECKS RUN, REMAINING BLOCKERS, ITERATION STATUS: COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE.
